addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- docs-consistency-guard: Documentation agent that audits docs for staleness and inconsistency AND generates/updates documentation on request. Use proactively when reviewing any PR that touches CLAUDE.md, docs/site/adr/, CONTRIBUTING.md, or docs/site/architecture/overview.md. Also invoke when the user asks "is the documentation up to date?", "update the milestone", "scaffold the ADR for X", "add this to the ADR index", "add a TODO item", "scaffold a README for X", or "create a doc stub for Y." (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit)

- driver-boundary-guard: Specialized reviewer for values that cross a DRIVER boundary — anything DataQ receives from a database connector, pyiceberg, pandas/pyarrow, or a cloud SDK and then type-narrows (isinstance / dtype checks / hasattr). Audits whether the covering tests hand-build the value in the shape our model expects (the "fixture encodes our model" defect that hid (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- mcp-honesty-reviewer: Specialized reviewer for DataQ's FastMCP tool surface (`backend/app/mcp/server.py`). Audits any new or changed tool's docstring and return payload against the nine honesty criteria drawn from 50+ real findings across the Tier-1 through Tier-3B builds — partial-as-final, unknown-as-zero, one null meaning two things, false (not just thin) docstrings, mutation-completion honesty, scope conflation, and stale sibling docstrings a new tool falsifies — plus a generic MCP-tool-quality pass (tool-selection honesty, safety annotations, unit ambiguity, unverified/forwarded data, silent input coercion, error-path actionability) independent of this repo's own issue history. Use proactively on every PR touching backend/app/mcp/server.py, and when the user asks "is this MCP tool honest about what it can't see?", "did this new tool age its neighbours?", or "does this tool meet a generic MCP client's expectations?". (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- migration-safety: Specialized reviewer for Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/. Audits for backward-incompatible operations that would break running code during a deploy, per working-agreement (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- orchestration-abstraction-guard: Specialized reviewer that audits backend code for provider-specific branching that bypasses the OrchestrationProvider abstraction. Use this proactively when reviewing any PR that touches backend/app/orchestration/, backend/app/services/, or backend/app/api/ — especially any code path handling ADF, Airflow or dbt events, trigger bindings, or pipeline_runs. Also invoke when the user asks "does this go through the abstraction?" or similar. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- qa-verifier: QA/QE agent that (1) runs the full local verification battery mirroring CI's required checks before any commit/push/PR, (2) audits test quality on changed code — failure-mode coverage, mocked-seam smells, coverage on changed files (Week-8 ≥80% gate), and (3) exercises the running application with data-level scenarios — authoring suites/checks through the real API, negative and edge-case inputs, authz probes — against the local stack's seeded demo data. Use proactively before pushing a branch or opening a PR, after writing or modifying tests, or when the user asks "run the gate", "is this ready to push?", "is this tested enough?", or "smoke the app with bad data". (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- regression-mutation-verifier: Proves that a new regression test actually fails against the unfixed code. Reverts the fix inside a throwaway git worktree, runs only the new test, and reports whether it fails for the RIGHT reason — catching tests that pass no matter what (the (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- ui-tester: End-to-end UI QA agent that exercises DataQ's frontend on BOTH desktop and mobile viewports (functionality + rendering) against the running app, AND audits backend↔frontend feature parity — flagging backend capabilities with no frontend surface (and frontend calls with no backend). Use when the user asks to "test the UI", "check mobile rendering", "find backend/frontend gaps", "is this feature wired end-to-end", or before a release. Drives a live browser via the Playwright MCP and reads code for the parity audit. (Tools: All tools)

## claude.ai Hugging Face
Hugging Face Hub MCP server for models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, and docs.
Prefer this connector's live Hub capabilities over the public website for all configured listings such as today's trending models, the current model leaderboard, daily papers, and paper popularity.

Use hf_fs for Hub filesystem and discovery:
- trending models: ls hf://models/trending
- trending datasets or Spaces: ls hf://datasets/trending, ls hf://spaces/trending
- trending papers / daily papers / paper of the day: ls hf://papers/trending, ls hf://papers/daily/latest
- search models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, or docs: search hf://models QUERY
- read a known file: cat hf://models/OWNER/NAME/README.md

Other advertised Hub tools can search or inspect a known repo id. Use hf_whoami for the current Hugging Face account.

hf:// URIs can be converted to browser URLs by replacing hf://buckets/OWNER/NAME/PATH with https://huggingface.co/buckets/OWNER/NAME/resolve/PATH; for models, datasets, and spaces, use https://huggingface.co[/datasets|/spaces]/OWNER/NAME/resolve/main/PATH. URL-encode each path segment.

arXiv paper ids (for example 2502.16161) are often used as references between datasets, models, and papers. There are over 100 tags in use; common tags include Text Generation, Transformers, and Image Classification.

## claude.ai Microsoft Learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- commit-commands:clean_gone: Cleans up all git branches marked as [gone] (branches that have been deleted on the remote but still exist locally), including removing associated worktrees.
- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- pr-review-toolkit:review-pr: Comprehensive PR review using specialized agents
- claude-code-setup:claude-automation-recommender: Analyze a codebase and recommend Claude Code automations (hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). Use when user asks for automation recommendations, wants to optimize their Claude Code setup, mentions improving Claude Code workflows, asks how to first set up Claude Code for a project, or wants to know what Claude Code features they should use.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- skill-creator:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

{"body":"The Admin page (#289) is one read-only scroll with two writes bolted on (role editor #1400, LLM settings #1641), while the backend and the planned feature set have outgrown it — four admin endpoints have no UI at all, and workspace membership, channels, and offboarding have no home. This epic tracks the redesign into a six-sub-page operations surface, per the 2026-08-29 design conversation.

**Mockup:** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e81272eb-4481-446f-8ea7-efa497493b92 (Overview · Members · Suites · Settings · Compliance · Integrations + the Add-member modal)

**Design principles (the durable part):**
1. Every read table earns a verb column — the page answers "is the workspace healthy, who can do what" and lets you act in place.
2. Routed, deep-linkable sub-pages with per-page data loading; route-gated, not button-hidden (#743 rule).
3. **Parity is a standing rule:** an admin endpoint with no UI is a defect; every admin-shaped feature ships its panel in the same PR.
4. Writes here are dangerous, so guard rails are the feature: G1 audit on every mutation, #1320 blast-radius confirmations, last-admin guards surfaced in UI.

## Build order

**Phase 1 — structure + parity (no new backend):**
- [ ] #1694 IA restructure — routed sub-pages
- [ ] #1695 parity pass — DSR / SMTP test / webhooks / chain verify

**Phase 2 — the write pass (the 'most powerful page' step):**
- [ ] #1693 in-app workspace membership (ADR 0043 to write first; IdP stays a prerequisite — user direction)
- [ ] #1698 manage any share · transfer ownership · admin delete
- [ ] #1699 offboarding flow (blocked by #1693 + #1698)

**Phase 3 — health + reach:**
- [ ] #1696 Overview workspace-health page
- [ ] #1697 datasource credential-health signal (backend; feeds #1696)
- [ ] #1700 workspace-wide admin lens on Dashboard/Results
- [ ] #1701 Integrations sub-page (secret regeneration, poll health, inventory sync)

**Absorbed as they land (their panels slot into Settings/Compliance):**
- [ ] #1514 notification channels — admin defines centrally, suites reference from a dropdown (model confirmed 2026-08-29; W5)
- [ ] #1676 zero-sample privacy mode toggle (W5)
- [ ] #1559 DQ scoring weights

**Related, not gated:** #1516 (Profile/Workspace-Settings IA — the non-admin settings sibling; keep the boundary explicit when picked up). Predecessors #412/#411 (closed in the v1.1 roll) are superseded by #1698/#1700; #954's re-file is #1697.

**Exit gate:** an admin can run the workspace end-to-end from /admin — admit and remove a member, hand off an owner's suites, rotate a webhook, answer a DSR request, and see every unhealthy thing on one page — with every mutation audited and every gate mutation-verified.","comments":[],"labels":["priority/P2","epic"],"milestone":"v1.2 Backlog","number":1702,"state":"OPEN","title":"Epic: Admin control centre — from read-only page to workspace operations surface"}

=== #1694 ===
1694 [OPEN] admin-ui(1): IA restructure — routed sub-pages (/admin/{overview,members,suites,settings,compliance,integrations}) | labels=enhancement,priority/P2 | ms=v1.2 Week 7 — feature burn-down
Phase 1 of the admin control-centre track (design conversation + mockup 2026-08-29: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e81272eb-4481-446f-8ea7-efa497493b92). Split the single-scroll /admin page into six routed, deep-linkable sub-pages rendered as tabs under the Admin title (the 220px sider stays untouched). Each sub-page loads its own data — today Admin.tsx fires every admin query at once on mount. Existing content re-homes: suites table → Suites, members/roles/access → Members, LLM settings → Settings, audit log + deployment posture → Compliance. Route gate stays `is_workspace_admin` (deep-linkable pages need their own gate — the #743 rule). No new backend.

=== #1695 ===
1695 [OPEN] admin-ui(2): parity pass — surface the four backend-only admin capabilities (DSR, SMTP test, webhooks, chain verify) | labels=enhancement,priority/P2 | ms=v1.2 Week 7 — feature burn-down
Four admin API endpoints exist with NO UI anywhere (verified 2026-08-29) — the backend↔frontend parity gaps the admin track's standing rule exists to prevent:
- **DSR export/erase** (G2, #1586): email input + Export / Erase with typed-address confirmation → Compliance sub-page.
- **SMTP pre-flight test** (`POST /admin/.../test_auth_email`, #1143): 'Send test email' button → Settings.
- **Orchestration webhooks listing** (`GET /admin/orchestration/webhooks`): table of provider endpoints + auth mode → Integrations.
- **Audit chain verify** (`GET /admin/audit-events/chain`): status card + 'Verify now' → Compliance.
All read/act against existing endpoints; no new backend. Mockup: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e81272eb-4481-446f-8ea7-efa497493b92. Standing rule this codifies: an admin endpoint with no UI is a defect, and every admin-shaped feature ships its panel in the same PR.

=== #1693 ===
1693 [OPEN] feat(admin): in-app workspace membership — admins add/remove members without touching env config (ADR 0043) | labels=enhancement,security,priority/P1 | ms=v1.2 Backlog
## Problem
An admin cannot add (or remove) a workspace member in DataQ. A user row is created lazily on first successful sign-in, and who may sign in is governed entirely by DEPLOYMENT ENV CONFIG: `OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS`/`_DOMAINS` (generic OIDC, #1386), `AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS`/`_DOMAINS` (OTP — the allowlist IS the member list), tenant membership (Azure AD). "Add Priya" = edit env vars + restart/redeploy + wait for her first login before a role can even be assigned. The Admin page manages roles of people already inside, not who gets in.

**Revocation is also inconsistent per door (verified 2026-08-29):** OIDC allowlist revokes per-request; OTP re-checks eligibility only at code request/redemption — a live `dq_sess_` session survives until TTL; a PAT never re-checks membership at all.

## Scope (user-directed 2026-08-29)
- **IdP account creation stays a prerequisite — we do NOT touch the IdP.** DataQ governs only its own door; the UI states this plainly for OIDC/Azure modes.
- New `workspace_members` table: normalized unique email, `initial_role`, invited_by, created_at. Admin CRUD at `/admin/members` (audited, G1).
- **Enforcement semantics:** DB table EMPTY → exactly today's behavior per mode (zero-migration-risk default). Table NON-EMPTY → union(env allowlist, DB rows) is the membership list, enforced per-request at the shared resolver choke points: `_upsert_user` (OIDC/Azure/MCP), `session_service.resolve_token` (OTP sessions), `api_key_service.resolve_token` (PATs, REST + MCP), `otp_service.is_signup_eligible` (both call sites). Dev-bypass exempt. This CLOSES the per-door revocation inconsistency — removal bites on the next request regardless of credential kind.
- Env allowlists demote to **bootstrap seed + break-glass, grant-only** — the ADR 0033 `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` pattern exactly.
- **Lockout guards:** the FIRST db row write auto-imports all existing users as members in the same transaction (turning enforcement on can never evict current users); removing the membership of the last admin-role user refuses (FOR UPDATE, mirroring #1400's last-admin guard); self-removal requires explicit confirm.
- **Pre-provisioned role:** `initial_role` seeds the user row at first sign-in (new-row branch only — the conflict branch stays promote-only per ADR 0033; the Members role editor remains authoritative after that).
- Frontend: Members & Access panel gains Add member (email + role), a pending-invites view (member rows with no user row yet), remove with the enforcement-state warning.

## Out of scope (recorded)
OTP invite emails (the code-request email already reaches them); IdP user provisioning; user deactivation/offboarding-transfer (#412's write pass); multi-workspace.

## Verification bar
Every choke point mutation-verified (a gate whose removal leaves the sweep green is not a gate — the #1424-class trap); the auto-import transactionality proven on real Postgres; revocation proven per credential kind (live session, live PAT) not just per door; superuser/commit test-blindness lessons apply (#1621).

Refs: #1386, ADR 0032/0033, #1400, #412 (the wider admin write pass), the 2026-08-29 admin-UI design conversation.

=== #1698 ===
1698 [OPEN] admin(4): write pass — manage any share, transfer suite ownership, admin delete with blast radius | labels=enhancement,priority/P2 | ms=v1.2 Backlog
Successor to #412 (closed in the v1.1 backlog roll) — the step that turns Admin from 'observes the workspace' into 'operates the workspace' (mockup: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e81272eb-4481-446f-8ea7-efa497493b92):
- **Manage/revoke any per-suite share** from the Members sub-page (today only the suite owner can, via the suite's own sharing panel).
- **Transfer suite ownership** (Suites sub-page) — the core offboarding primitive.
- **Admin delete of any suite** reusing the #1320 blast-radius confirmation (N checks / runs / results, irreversibility stated).
All three are new admin-scoped mutations: audit events (G1 coverage table), `FOR UPDATE` where ordering matters, and RBAC sweeps whose denial probes are mutation-verified (the vacuous-pass trap, four occurrences on record).

=== #1699 ===
1699 [OPEN] admin(5): offboarding flow — deactivate a user, transfer their suites, revoke their PATs in one guided pass | labels=enhancement,priority/P3 | ms=v1.2 Backlog
The composed flow on top of the write pass (#1694-track) + membership (#1693): 'Olivia is leaving' → one guided action that (1) removes/deactivates membership so her next request fails regardless of credential kind, (2) walks suite-ownership transfer for everything she owns (the #1694-track transfer primitive, batched), (3) revokes her `dq_live_` PATs, (4) leaves her authored history intact (`created_by` rows survive — ondelete=SET NULL discipline already in place). Guards: last-admin refusal, typed confirmation, every step audited. Blocked by #1693 + the write-pass issue.

=== #1696 ===
1696 [OPEN] admin-ui(3): Overview — the workspace health page (needs-attention feed + health signals) | labels=enhancement,priority/P2 | ms=v1.2 Backlog
The 'morning page' of the admin control centre (mockup: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e81272eb-4481-446f-8ea7-efa497493b92): stat cards (members, suites, open incidents, runs today) + a needs-attention feed + health checks, each linking to the thing that needs fixing. Signals to compose:
- Dead orchestration polls — `workspace_health` (#1100) already tracks this.
- Datasource credential health — needs the re-filed #954 signal (separate backend issue, blocks this row only).
- Orphan-secret sweep — report exists (#1070); needs a read endpoint + 'run now'.
- Audit chain status — endpoint exists.
- Beat heartbeat / queue depth — worker-side signal, small read API.
Ship incrementally: rows light up as their signal exists; a missing signal renders as 'not monitored', never silently absent (#828 rule).

=== #1697 ===
1697 [OPEN] connections: datasource credential-health signal — a dead credential is invisible until a run fails (re-file of #954's general half) | labels=enhancement,priority/P2 | ms=v1.2 Backlog
#954 (closed 2026-07-25) documented the incident — two dead Snowflake PATs discoverable only via worker logs — but its closure comment explicitly flags that the GENERAL datasource-credential health surface was never tracked anywhere and 'should be re-filed rather than considered done'. This is that re-file.

#839's health signal covers orchestration connections only; #1100's staleness axis covers lineage-refreshing connections. A plain datasource connection with a rotten credential has no visible state anywhere (the #828 blindness class). Ship: a lightweight periodic credential probe (or piggyback on run outcomes: consecutive auth-failure classification per connection), surfaced on the connections list + the admin Overview feed. An unprobed connection reads 'unknown', never 'healthy'.

=== #1700 ===
1700 [OPEN] admin(6): workspace-wide admin lens on Dashboard + Results (successor of #411) | labels=enhancement,priority/P3 | ms=v1.2 Backlog
Successor to #411 (closed in the v1.1 backlog roll). Dashboard + Results are owned-or-shared scoped for everyone, admins included — a workspace admin cannot see the health of suites not shared with them without going to the Admin suites table. Design decision from the 2026-08-29 conversation: an explicit 'admin lens' TOGGLE on the existing pages (badge visible while on, default off) rather than a copy of the pages inside Admin — one implementation, no drift, and the scope switch is deliberate + auditable (a phase-2 G1 read-event covers it).

=== #1701 ===
1701 [OPEN] admin-ui(7): Integrations sub-page — webhook secret regeneration + polling health + inventory-sync surface | labels=enhancement,priority/P3 | ms=v1.2 Backlog
The Integrations sub-page of the admin control centre (mockup: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e81272eb-4481-446f-8ea7-efa497493b92), beyond the read-only webhook listing (#1695):
- **Regenerate webhook secret/HMAC key** per provider (new mutation; audited; the old key keeps working for a short grace window so the provider-side update isn't a race).
- **Polling health table** — last poll / stalled / next poll per orchestration connection (reads `workspace_health` #1100 + poll bookkeeping).
- **Inventory sync surface** (ADR 0040) — per-connection toggle + last sync + tables discovered + unmonitored count, today configurable only via the connection editor.
'Poll all now' fires the existing immediate-poll path.

=== #1514 ===
1514 [CLOSED] feat(alerting): reusable notification channels — define a Teams/Slack/email channel once, reference from many suites | labels=enhancement | ms=v1.2 Week 5 — native engines (DMF) + notification channels
From [docs/post-v1-admin-ui-notes.md](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/docs/post-v1-admin-ui-notes.md) §'What to keep building' — the one item in that (otherwise ADR-0033-superseded) doc still unbuilt and untracked.

Today notification config is **per suite** (`suite_notifications`: `webhook_secret_ref` + `slack_webhook_secret_ref` + `email_recipients`). A real platform DQ feature is a first-class **channel** entity: define a Teams/Slack/email destination once, reference it from many suites (and severities); rotating a webhook then touches one place instead of N suites.

Notes:
- Build as a **notification feature, not an admin-console feature** (the doc's explicit guidance).
- #389 (channel-neutral rename) already closed; this is the entity/reuse half.
- Channel secrets stay `SecretStore` refs; the orphan-secret sweep's ownership registry must learn the new ref location (the lesson from 2026-07-27: Slack/Teams refs on one row were mis-registered once already).
- Keep per-suite `alert_on`/severity routing — the channel is the destination, not the policy.

=== #1676 ===
1676 [CLOSED] feat(privacy): zero-sample "privacy mode" — deployment-level switch, failing-row samples never persisted | labels=enhancement,security,priority/P2 | ms=v1.2 Week 5 — native engines (DMF) + notification channels
Theme-4 privacy pack, item 3 (verified 2026-08-29: nothing in backend/app implements this yet). A deployment-level switch where failing-row samples are NEVER persisted — aggregates + metric_value + unexpected-counts only. Mostly a write-path gate at result persistence; turns the existing redaction stack into a tiered posture: full → column-aware redacted (#417) → zero-sample. The first question HIPAA-tier / EU deployments ask. Must gate every sample writer (results JSONB, dry-run, MCP dryrun_check, alerts) — the guard-at-one-door-not-its-sibling class is the known failure mode here.

=== #1559 ===
1559 [OPEN] Admin-configurable DQ scoring weights (workspace-level ScoringConfig, audit-logged) | labels=enhancement | ms=v1.2 Week 7 — feature burn-down
## What
`rollup.health_score` (`backend/app/services/rollup.py:20-49`) hardcodes severity weights — `pass=0, warn=0.5, fail=1.0, critical=2.0` — used identically at every level (check, suite, per-asset dimension, workspace-windowed). No org-level tuning exists; every deployment gets the same risk model.

## Scope (as directed)
- A **workspace-level `ScoringConfig`** (severity weights at minimum; consider a "critical = hard 0 regardless of other counts" toggle as a stretch), admin-only to edit — same access tier as other workspace-wide settings.
- `health_score` takes the weights as a parameter instead of the hardcoded module constant; every call site (dashboard, suite performance, asset scorecard) reads the active config.
- **Every change is audit-logged** (ADR 0041 / G1) — an admin silently changing what "healthy" means workspace-wide is exactly the kind of action that audit trail exists for. This also gives the audit-log UI (#1554) a second real consumer once that ships.

## Design decision that must be made explicit, not a side effect
`health_score` is computed **live, on read** — nothing is stored. If weights become editable, every historical score displayed anywhere (including trend charts) recolors the instant an admin changes them, with no data-side change to explain the step. That may be the right behavior (an "always current lens" is defensible), but it must be a stated decision in the implementing PR/ADR, not something discovered after the fact. The alternative — snapshotting the weights (or the computed score) at run time — is a real design fork worth writing down and picking deliberately.

## Found via
Design discussion following the #1550–#1555 backend↔frontend parity work (session 2026-08-22).

=== #1516 ===
1516 [OPEN] feat(ui): Profile / Workspace-Settings IA pickup — replace the labelled placeholders (deferred-by-design) | labels=enhancement | ms=v1.2 Week 7 — feature burn-down
From [docs/post-v1-admin-ui-notes.md](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/blob/main/docs/post-v1-admin-ui-notes.md) §'Settings / Profile page'. Filed so the deferral is tracker-visible (the #466/#244 deferred-by-design precedent), not because it is due: the doc's own call is 'low-value polish right now — defer'.

When picked up:
- **Profile:** identity, the user's owned suites, an access summary (display-name editing shipped with OTP #1153; the rest are Week-6 labelled placeholders from #374).
- **Workspace Settings:** notification channels (see the reusable-channels issue), run-history retention, the admin allowlist surfaced read-only (#375 placeholders).
- Theme / timezone / dark-mode stay out unless users ask (ADR 0022).

=== #1320 ===
1320 [CLOSED] feat(suites): suite-delete confirmation must state its blast radius (N checks / runs / results destroyed) | labels=enhancement,priority/P3 | ms=v1.2 Week 2 — expectation catalog + server-side allowlist
From ADR [0041](../blob/main/docs/adr/0041-history-audit-strategy.md) §2 decision 3 — this is the mitigation that makes re-deferring soft-delete honest rather than a bare "no".

## Problem

`DELETE /api/v1/suites/{id}` cascades **checks → runs → results** (`runs.suite_id` and `results.check_id`/`run_id` are all `ON DELETE CASCADE` since #540). There is no soft-delete, no retention copy, and no undo: a suite with two years of run history is destroyed by one confirmation dialog that says nothing about it.

This is the one place where ADR 0020's accepted cascade posture still costs real, irreplaceable data — the connection half was closed by the #753 409 guard (a connection with suites simply cannot be deleted), leaving suite deletion as the only path to silent history loss.

ADR 0041 re-defers soft-delete for good reasons (a `deleted_at IS NULL` predicate across an asset/lineage/incident/rollup query surface; "deleted means inert" for live SecretStore credentials, trigger bindings and schedules; and a delete-that-does-not-delete working against #432/G2 erasure). What it does **not** defend is the user finding out afterwards.

## Fix

Make the blast radius explicit **before** the fact:

- `GET /suites/{id}` (or a small dedicated endpoint) returns the dependent counts: checks, runs, results, plus whether any trigger binding or schedule points at the suite.
- The delete confirmation states them plainly — e.g. *"Deletes 12 checks, 431 runs and 5,180 results. This cannot be undone."* — rather than the current generic confirm.
- Counts are computed, never estimated; if a count is capped for cost, say so (no silent caps).

Deliberately **not** in scope: undo, soft-delete, archive/export-on-delete. Those re-open ADR 0041 §2.3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dependent counts (checks / runs / results / trigger bindings / schedules) available to the frontend for a suite the caller may delete
- [ ] Suite delete confirmation shows the counts and states that it is irreversible
- [ ] Authz unchanged — counts follow the same grant as the delete itself, no leak to a `view`-only user
- [ ] Test: a suite with runs shows non-zero counts; a never-run suite shows zeros and does not degrade to a scary-but-empty warning


=== #743 ===
743 [CLOSED] feat(rbac): role-aware frontend — connections read-only for non-admins, viewer UX, role E2E per perspective (ADR 0033) | labels=enhancement,priority/P2 | ms=v1.1 Backlog
Implementation slice of **ADR 0033 — workspace roles (RBAC)**; see the umbrella issue.

## Scope — role-aware frontend

1. **`useMe` plumbs `role`** (alongside `is_workspace_admin`); the server stays the decider — the UI only mirrors (same principle as the per-suite level stamping).
2. **Connections page**: create/edit/delete/re-auth controls hidden for non-admins; read-only presentation for members/viewers with a hint ("managed by workspace admins").
3. **Viewer UX**: suite-create/import controls hidden; share dialog doesn't offer `edit` for viewer grantees (mirrors the backend rejection, which stays authoritative).
4. **Admin UI Users tab**: role column + editor wiring (backend contract from the management slice), incl. the last-admin guard error state.
5. **E2E**: Playwright specs per role — admin (full), member (no connection mutations), viewer (read-only shell) — using the dev-bypass/seeded users approach the existing specs use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All gating derives from `/me` role; no client-side-only "security"
- [ ] Vitest coverage holds the 80% all-src gate
- [ ] Three role-perspective Playwright specs green in CI
- [ ] Feature-matrix / user docs updated with the role capability table

"Add Priya" = edit env vars + restart/redeploy + wait for her first login before a role can even be assigned. The Admin page manages roles of people already inside, not who gets in.

**Revocation is also inconsistent per door (verified 2026-08-29):** OIDC allowlist revokes per-request; OTP re-checks eligibility only at code request/redemption — a live `dq_sess_` session survives until TTL; a PAT never re-checks membership at all.

## Scope (user-directed 2026-08-29)
- **IdP account creation stays a prerequisite — we do NOT touch the IdP.** DataQ governs only its own door; the UI states this plainly for OIDC/Azure modes.
- New `workspace_members` table: normalized unique email, `initial_role`, invited_by, created_at. Admin CRUD at `/admin/members` (audited, G1).
- **Enforcement semantics:** DB table EMPTY → exactly today's behavior per mode (zero-migration-risk default). Table NON-EMPTY → union(env allowlist, DB rows) is the membership list, enforced per-request at the shared resolver choke points: `_upsert_user` (OIDC/Azure/MCP), `session_service.resolve_token` (OTP sessions), `api_key_service.resolve_token` (PATs, REST + MCP), `otp_service.is_signup_eligible` (both call sites). Dev-bypass exempt. This CLOSES the per-door revocation inconsistency — removal bites on the next request regardless of credential kind.
- Env allowlists demote to **bootstrap seed + break-glass, grant-only** — the ADR 0033 `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` pattern exactly.
- **Lockout guards:** the FIRST db row write auto-imports all existing users as members in the same transaction (turning enforcement on can never evict current users); removing the membership of the last admin-role user refuses (FOR UPDATE, mirroring #1400's last-admin guard); self-removal requires explicit confirm.
- **Pre-provisioned role:** `initial_role` seeds the user row at first sign-in (new-row branch only — the conflict branch stays promote-only per ADR 0033; the Members role editor remains authoritative after that).
- Frontend: Members & Access panel gains Add member (email + role), a pending-invites view (member rows with no user row yet), remove with the enforcement-state warning.

## Out of scope (recorded)
OTP invite emails (the code-request email already reaches them); IdP user provisioning; user deactivation/offboarding-transfer (#412's write pass); multi-workspace.

## Verification bar
Every choke point mutation-verified (a gate whose removal leaves the sweep green is not a gate — the #1424-class trap); the auto-import transactionality proven on real Postgres; revocation proven per credential kind (live session, live PAT) not just per door; superuser/commit test-blindness lessons apply (#1621).

Refs: #1386, ADR 0032/0033, #1400, #412 (the wider admin write pass), the 2026-08-29 admin-UI design conversation.

=== #1559 ===
1559 [OPEN] Admin-configurable DQ scoring weights (workspace-level ScoringConfig, audit-logged) | labels=enhancement | ms=v1.2 Week 7 — feature burn-down
## What
`rollup.health_score` (`backend/app/services/rollup.py:20-49`) hardcodes severity weights — `pass=0, warn=0.5, fail=1.0, critical=2.0` — used identically at every level (check, suite, per-asset dimension, workspace-windowed). No org-level tuning exists; every deployment gets the same risk model.

## Scope (as directed)
- A **workspace-level `ScoringConfig`** (severity weights at minimum; consider a "critical = hard 0 regardless of other counts" toggle as a stretch), admin-only to edit — same access tier as other workspace-wide settings.
- `health_score` takes the weights as a parameter instead of the hardcoded module constant; every call site (dashboard, suite performance, asset scorecard) reads the active config.
- **Every change is audit-logged** (ADR 0041 / G1) — an admin silently changing what "healthy" means workspace-wide is exactly the kind of action that audit trail exists for. This also gives the audit-log UI (#1554) a second real consumer once that ships.

## Design decision that must be made explicit, not a side effect
`health_score` is computed **live, on read** — nothing is stored. If weights become editable, every historical score displayed anywhere (including trend charts) recolors the instant an admin changes them, with no data-side change to explain the step. That may be the right behavior (an "always current lens" is defensible), but it must be a stated decision in the implementing PR/ADR, not something discovered after the fact. The alternative — snapshotting the weights (or the computed score) at run time — is a real design fork worth writing down and picking deliberately.

Design discussion following the #1550–#1555 backend↔frontend parity work (session 2026-08-22).

=== #1320 ===
1320 [CLOSED] feat(suites): suite-delete confirmation must state its blast radius (N checks / runs / results destroyed) | labels=enhancement,priority/P3 | ms=v1.2 Week 2 — expectation catalog + server-side allowlist
From ADR [0041](../blob/main/docs/adr/0041-history-audit-strategy.md) §2 decision 3 — this is the mitigation that makes re-deferring soft-delete honest rather than a bare "no".

## Problem

`DELETE /api/v1/suites/{id}` cascades **checks → runs → results** (`runs.suite_id` and `results.check_id`/`run_id` are all `ON DELETE CASCADE` since #540). There is no soft-delete, no retention copy, and no undo: a suite with two years of run history is destroyed by one confirmation dialog that says nothing about it.

This is the one place where ADR 0020's accepted cascade posture still costs real, irreplaceable data — the connection half was closed by the #753 409 guard (a connection with suites simply cannot be deleted), leaving suite deletion as the only path to silent history loss.

ADR 0041 re-defers soft-delete for good reasons (a `deleted_at IS NULL` predicate across an asset/lineage/incident/rollup query surface; "deleted means inert" for live SecretStore credentials, trigger bindings and schedules; and a delete-that-does-not-delete working against #432/G2 erasure). What it does **not** defend is the user finding out afterwards.

## Fix

Make the blast radius explicit **before** the fact:

- `GET /suites/{id}` (or a small dedicated endpoint) returns the dependent counts: checks, runs, results, plus whether any trigger binding or schedule points at the suite.
- The delete confirmation states them plainly — e.g. *"Deletes 12 checks, 431 runs and 5,180 results. This cannot be undone."* — rather than the current generic confirm.
- Counts are computed, never estimated; if a count is capped for cost, say so (no silent caps).

Deliberately **not** in scope: undo, soft-delete, archive/export-on-delete. Those re-open ADR 0041 §2.3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dependent counts (checks / runs / results / trigger bindings / schedules) available to the frontend for a suite the caller may delete
- [ ] Suite delete confirmation shows the counts and states that it is irreversible
- [ ] Authz unchanged — counts follow the same grant as the delete itself, no leak to a `view`-only user
- [ ] Test: a suite with runs shows non-zero counts; a never-run suite shows zeros and does not degrade to a scary-but-empty warning

| [0038](0038-dq-dimension-classification.md) | DQ-dimension classification on checks — **seven canonical dimensions** (accuracy/completeness/consistency/integrity/timeliness/uniqueness/validity) as a **closed** vocabulary via table `CHECK`, not a Postgres ENUM (no `ALTER TYPE` friction) and not free text (unbounded values destroy coverage reporting); **derived default → stored → overridable at any time** (stored so the scorecard aggregates in SQL and an override survives); derivation is **deliberately partial** — `accuracy`/`integrity` are never derived and custom SQL has no answer, so **NULL means unclassified** and the scorecard must render it as a gap; **existing rows ARE backfilled** (migration `a7b8c9d0e1f2`; §5 **amended 2026-07-19** — the backfill cannot overwrite a human decision because none existed yet when it ran, while leaving them NULL made the scorecard useless on day one; unmapped types stay NULL); `dimension` ⊥ `kind` ⊥ `engine`; narrows 0036 §4 — lands the derivation map as the backend catalog's seed without moving the frontend catalog server-side, since no native engine exists yet | Accepted |
| [0039](0039-openbao-self-hosted-secret-backend.md) | Self-hosted secret backend — a fourth `SecretStore` speaking the **KV v2 HTTP API, not a vendor SDK** (one mode serves OpenBao / Vault Community / Enterprise / HCP; no HashiCorp lock-in traded for the Azure one); **OpenBao** (MPL-2.0, LF fork of pre-BUSL Vault 1.14) is the shipped/tested/pinned server — Vault Community is BUSL-1.1 and rule-40-forbidden as a *distributed* component, supported as a *target*; **`SECRET_STORE=openbao` replaces `redis` and `RedisSecretStore` is deleted** (plaintext credentials were the default of the published eval stack), with a loud one-cycle `RuntimeError` shim, **Redis stays** for broker + rate-limit counters; token auth phase 1 (AppRole deferred/filed), dev-mode token generated into the gitignored `.env`; Azure Key Vault remains the prod default (managed identity beats a held token), OpenBao is the BYOL/cloud-neutral option; **an outage is never reportable as a state** — new `SecretStoreUnavailableError`, deliberately NOT a `SecretNotFoundError` subclass, since every caller branches on the TYPE and none reads the message (a sealed vault otherwise renders "not set" on the admin page, skips alert delivery silently, and runs connections with the credential omitted); no status is silent (400=KV v1 mount, 401=gateway, 429=HCP throttle); **`AzureKeyVaultStore` had the same defect since Week 2** and is fixed too (the same invisible-degradation shape seen before); `delete` purges via KV v2 **metadata** delete, fail-soft | Accepted |
| [0040](0040-warehouse-inventory-sync-table-enumeration-seam.md) | Warehouse inventory sync + the **table-enumeration seam** — one per-datasource `enumerate_tables` capability (Snowflake/UC `information_schema`, engine-native case = the identity-safe path, connection-database scoping, ephemera/system schemas excluded) feeding three consumers: **inventory sync** (opt-in per connection, daily crontab beat, `upsert_assets(preserve_provenance=True)` so `last_seen` advancement keeps live tables out of the orphan sweep and dropped tables age out through it — no new column, no new guard; no "discovered" badge, ADR 0037's neutral unmonitored rendering IS the marker), **GET_LINEAGE seeds**, and future pickers; `ASSET_INVENTORY_MAX_TABLES` cap (default 2000) with loud truncation; **decided**: S3 namespace stays `s3://{bucket}` for AWS, becomes `s3://{host[:port]}/{bucket}` only when `endpoint_url` is set | Accepted |
| [0041](0041-history-audit-strategy.md) | History & audit posture for v1.x+ (amends 0020) — **one append-only `audit_events` table** (actor/action/entity/before/after/ts) recording **deliberate acts by a principal only**, with `entity_id` deliberately **FK-less** so the row outlives the entity it describes (an FK would either cascade the audit away or block the delete); the data-**read** audit (gap G1) is **phase 2 on the same table**, discriminated by `action_class` — not a second table — with the opposite latency contract (phase 1 writes inside the mutation's transaction, fail-closed; phase-2 reads must stay off the critical path); **(a) preserving `check_versions` past delete rejected** — `RESTRICT` makes checks undeletable, `SET NULL` orphans rows needing self-contained identity (a worse audit log scoped to one entity), tombstone = soft-delete for one table — the audit log's delete event answers it instead and **cascade stands**; **(b) soft-delete re-deferred** on a narrowed argument (its headline motivation is already met — an earlier 409 guard means a connection can no longer be deleted out from under its runs; the column is the easy part vs. "deleted means inert" for live credentials/bindings/schedules; and a delete-that-doesn't-delete fights the G2 Art-17 erasure work), mitigated by a follow-up blast-radius confirmation; **(d) SCD-2 closed permanently**, not deferred; Type-4 tables stay the **product** surface (version drawer/restore), the audit log is the **durable record**; payloads are **per-entity allow-lists** reusing the snapshot builders, never `dict(row)`, never a secret value, never `sample_failures`/`observed_value`, and reuse only the **credential subset** of `_PII_KEYS` (the full set redacts `name`/`display_name`/`user_id` — the very content of a rename and the point of the actor record); append-only via `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` — **a guard against accidental in-app mutation, explicitly NOT tamper-resistance** (`dataq_app` owns the table and can re-grant; splitting the role is rejected because the single-role model is the whole mitigation for the unpatched Postgres RI owner-cast escalation, so real tamper-evidence needs the G1 external anchor); coverage guarded off FastAPI's **route table**, not an audit registry (the ADR-0039 tautology) | Accepted (phase-1 build; follow-ups filed) |

| [0041](0041-history-audit-strategy.md) | History & audit posture for v1.x+ (amends 0020) — **one append-only `audit_events` table** (actor/action/entity/before/after/ts) recording **deliberate acts by a principal only**, with `entity_id` deliberately **FK-less** so the row outlives the entity it describes (an FK would either cascade the audit away or block the delete); the data-**read** audit (gap G1) is **phase 2 on the same table**, discriminated by `action_class` — not a second table — with the opposite latency contract (phase 1 writes inside the mutation's transaction, fail-closed; phase-2 reads must stay off the critical path); **(a) preserving `check_versions` past delete rejected** — `RESTRICT` makes checks undeletable, `SET NULL` orphans rows needing self-contained identity (a worse audit log scoped to one entity), tombstone = soft-delete for one table — the audit log's delete event answers it instead and **cascade stands**; and a delete-that-doesn't-delete fights the G2 Art-17 erasure work), mitigated by a follow-up blast-radius confirmation; **(d) SCD-2 closed permanently**, not deferred; Type-4 tables stay the **product** surface (version drawer/restore), the audit log is the **durable record**; payloads are **per-entity allow-lists** reusing the snapshot builders, never `dict(row)`, never a secret value, never `sample_failures`/`observed_value`, and reuse only the **credential subset** of `_PII_KEYS` (the full set redacts `name`/`display_name`/`user_id` — the very content of a rename and the point of the actor record); append-only via `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` — **a guard against accidental in-app mutation, explicitly NOT tamper-resistance** (`dataq_app` owns the table and can re-grant; splitting the role is rejected because the single-role model is the whole mitigation for the unpatched Postgres RI owner-cast escalation, so real tamper-evidence needs the G1 external anchor); coverage guarded off FastAPI's **route table**, not an audit registry (the ADR-0039 tautology) | Accepted (phase-1 build; follow-ups filed) |

## 1. Frontend Admin page

**Route & gating**
- `frontend/src/App.tsx:56` lazy-imports `Admin`; `frontend/src/App.tsx:265` — `<Route path="/admin" element={<Admin />} />`. Flat, single route, **no nested routes/tabs today**.

- `frontend/src/auth/useMe.ts` exports `useMe`, `useUpdateMe`, `useIsWorkspaceAdmin`, `useWorkspaceRole`, `useCanMutateConnections`, `useCanAuthor`. Context in `frontend/src/auth/meContext.ts`, provider `frontend/src/auth/MeProvider.tsx`. There is also `frontend/src/auth/RequireRole.tsx` (used for connection/suite routes at `App.tsx:222-255`) but it is **not** applied to `/admin`.

**Sections rendered** (`Admin.tsx`, 533 lines, one long scroll — the vitest name literally says "no tabs"):
1. Three `MetricCard`s: Suites / Members / Access grants (`Admin.tsx:81-107`)
2. "All suites" table (`:112`)
3. "Members & access" — users table with inline `RoleEditor`, plus a second access-grants table (`:120-138`)

5. `<DeploymentPostureSection />` (`:139`, impl ~`:338`)

**API calls on mount** (all via `useAsyncData`): `listAdminSuites`, `listAdminUsers`, `listAdminAccess` (`Admin.tsx:70-72`), `listAuditEvents` (`:189`), `getDeploymentPosture` (`:338`), plus the LLM panel's own `getLlmConfig`.

**Related modules**: `frontend/src/api/admin.ts` (164 lines — suites/users/access/role/webhooks/auth-email-test/audit-events/deployment), `frontend/src/api/llm.ts` (the `/admin/llm*` calls live here, *not* in admin.ts), `frontend/src/api/me.ts:24`, `frontend/src/api/notificationChannels.ts`. **Tests**: `frontend/tests/pages/Admin.test.tsx` (10 cases incl. forbidden-path "fetches nothing", pager-refetch, filter-submission semantics), `frontend/tests/api/adminMe.test.ts`, e2e `frontend/e2e/admin.spec.ts` (4 tests) and `frontend/e2e/roles.spec.ts:71` ("member is not offered the admin page"). Backend: `backend/tests/api/test_admin.py`, `test_admin_llm.py`, `test_admin_role_management.py`, `test_admin_data_subject_requests.py`.

## 2. Backend admin API

`backend/app/api/v1/admin.py` — one router, `prefix="/admin"`, **router-level `dependencies=[Depends(require_workspace_admin)]`** (`admin.py:33-37`); mounted at `backend/app/main.py:230` under `/api/v1`. Write routes additionally take `current_user: Depends(require_workspace_admin)` as a *parameter* (they need the actor identity for auditing, not extra gating).

| # | Method | Path | Line | Service |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | GET | `/admin/suites` | `:86` | `admin_service.all_suites` |
| 2 | GET | `/admin/users` | `:91` | `admin_service` users |
| 3 | GET | `/admin/access` | `:96` | `admin_service` access |
| 4 | PATCH | `/admin/users/{user_id}/role` | `:109` | role mgmt (ADR 0033, #742) |
| 5 | GET | `/admin/orchestration/webhooks` | `:138` | + `SecretStore` (#490) |

| 7 | GET | `/admin/llm` | `:238` | llm settings |

| 9 | POST | `/admin/llm/test` | `:269` | live probe, audited (#1773) |

| 11 | GET | `/admin/audit-events/verify` | `:401` | `verify_audit_chain` |
| 12 | GET | `/admin/deployment` | `:534` | posture, incl. `zero_sample_mode` |
| 13 | POST | `/admin/data-subject-requests/export` | `:701` | GDPR Art 15/20 |
| 14 | POST | `/admin/data-subject-requests/erase` | `:784` | GDPR Art 17 |

## 3. Backend admin endpoints with NO frontend caller

Grepped all of `frontend/src` per path. **Four orphans** — which matches the already-filed issue #1695 "parity pass (4 backend-only admin endpoints)":

- `GET /admin/audit-events/verify` — zero hits anywhere in `frontend/`. The chain-verify button does not exist.
- `POST /admin/data-subject-requests/export` — zero hits (documented as a curl runbook only, `docs/site/security/compliance/data-subject-rights-runbook.md:40`)
- `POST /admin/data-subject-requests/erase` — zero hits (`…runbook.md:60`)
- `GET /api/v1/orchestration/near-misses` — not admin-prefixed but admin-scoped (`backend/app/api/v1/runs.py:525-556`, `include_all=is_workspace_admin(...)`); no frontend caller found.

Also worth noting for the redesign: two admin endpoints are called from **Settings**, not Admin — `listAdminWebhooks` (`frontend/src/pages/Settings.tsx:155`) and `testAuthEmail` (`Settings.tsx:79`). So the admin surface is currently split across `/admin` and `/settings` with no clear rule.

## 4. Notification channels (#1761) + zero-sample mode (#1676/#1873)

- Channel UI lives at **`/settings` → "Notifications" tab**, not `/admin`: `frontend/src/pages/Settings.tsx:22,134` mounts `components/admin/NotificationChannelsPanel.tsx` (note the file is in `components/admin/` while rendering under Settings). Effectively admin-only because the whole Settings page is gated (`Settings.tsx:46`).
- Backend `backend/app/api/v1/notification_channels.py:25` — router has **no** `/admin` prefix and uses `get_current_user`, with admin enforcement inside `channel_service` for the mutating routes (panel comment at `NotificationChannelsPanel.tsx:41-43` says "Channel CRUD is Admin-only server-side"). Routes: GET/POST `/notification-channels`, GET/PATCH/DELETE `/notification-channels/{id}`, and the per-suite link set GET/PUT/DELETE `/suites/{id}/notification-channels[/{channelId}]`.
- **Zero-sample mode is env-only**: `backend/app/core/config.py:109` `privacy_zero_sample_mode: bool = False` (`PRIVACY_ZERO_SAMPLE_MODE`). No write API. It is only *readable* via `GET /admin/deployment` → `zero_sample_mode`, surfaced read-only in `DeploymentPostureSection`. Docs note both api and worker processes must restart to flip it (`get_settings()` is a per-process `lru_cache`) — so an admin-UI toggle would need that constraint designed around.

## 5. workspace_health (#1100) / orphan-secret sweep (#1070)

- Table `workspace_health` at `backend/app/db/models.py:1030-1035`; service `backend/app/services/workspace_health_service.py` (keys: `POLL_STALENESS_KEY` at `:34`, `trigger_env_near_miss:*`). Poll-staleness check wired at `backend/app/main.py:62`.
- **Only partial read API**: `GET /api/v1/orchestration/near-misses` (`backend/app/api/v1/runs.py:525`) exposes the `trigger_env_near_miss:*` rows. The **poll-staleness signal has no read endpoint at all** — a natural fit for the #1696 Overview health page.
- **Orphan-secret sweep has no API whatsoever**: `backend/app/services/secret_sweep_service.py` (`find_orphan_secrets:112`, `sweep_orphan_secrets:139`) is invoked only from the Celery beat schedule `sweep-orphan-secrets` (`backend/app/worker/celery_app.py:130-133`), reporting-only unless `SECRET_ORPHAN_PURGE`. Findings are log-only; nothing is persisted to `workspace_health` and nothing is queryable.

## 6. Routing / tabs conventions to follow

- Tabs are **antd `<Tabs>` with `defaultActiveKey` + `items[]`, state-local, not URL-backed**. Two precedents: `frontend/src/pages/Results.tsx:103-119` (runs / pipelines) and `frontend/src/pages/Settings.tsx:55-64` (general / secrets / webhooks / notifications / danger). Neither syncs to the URL, so a tab is not linkable or reload-stable today.
- Nested *routes* are done as flat sibling paths, not `<Outlet>` children — e.g. `/suites/:suiteId`, `/suites/:suiteId/edit`, `/suites/:suiteId/checks/new` (`App.tsx:256-259`). Suite "detail" reuses the `Suites` page component with a param rather than a child route.
- So for #1694's six routed sub-pages there is **no existing routed-tab pattern to copy** — you would be establishing it. Closest existing gate pattern to reuse: `frontend/src/auth/RequireRole.tsx` as used at `App.tsx:222-255`, which would let `/admin/*` be guarded at the route level instead of the current in-component check.
- Standard page scaffolding: `components/layout/Page`, `components/feedback/PageError`, `components/Forbidden`, `components/AsyncBody`, and the `useAsyncData` / `useAsyncAction` hook pair (`useAsyncData` does **not** auto-refetch on dep change — it exposes `reload()`, which `AuditLogSection` has to bump manually; a known sharp edge for a filter-heavy redesign).

## 7. Docs

- `docs/post-v1-admin-ui-notes.md` — **does not exist**. Nearest sibling is `docs/post-v1-dq-intelligence-notes.md`.
- `docs/site/guides/` — **no admin guide**. Files: ai-features, api-keys, best-practices, datasources-checks, features, index, mcp-setup, notifications, orchestration, recommended-usage, scheduling.
- `docs/site/security/overview.md` admin sections: SMTP pre-flight (`:51-71`), env-allowlist admin escalation warning (`:151-157`), audit-events (`:161`), zero-sample mode (`:240-244`), deployment posture / residency (`:447-465`).
- ADRs: **0033** `docs/site/adr/0033-workspace-roles-rbac.md` and **0041** `docs/site/adr/0041-history-audit-strategy.md` both exist. **0043 does not exist** — 0042 (`llm-provider-seam`) is the highest. `context/roadmap-v1.2-v1.3.md:95-103` records that ADR 0043 is *to be written* for #1693 (in-app membership), with IdP as a stated prerequisite.
- Also relevant: `docs/site/adr/0027-suite-permission-model-workspace-admin.md`, `docs/site/security/compliance/data-subject-rights-runbook.md` (the manual curl workflow the missing DSR UI would replace).

**Prior planning already on file** (`docs/progress.md:30`, `context/roadmap-v1.2-v1.3.md:36,95-103`): epic **#1702** admin control-centre with six routed sub-pages and a published mockup (2026-08-29), over #1693 membership, #1694 IA restructure, #1695 parity pass (the 4 orphan endpoints above), #1696 Overview health page, #1697 credential health, #1698 write pass, #1699 offboarding, #1700 admin lens, #1701 Integrations. Worth reading before designing, since the sequencing is already user-directed.</result>

PR #1889 review left four inline comments (r3938959456, r3938959493, r3938959511, r3938959546). Revise the ADR with a follow-up `fixup:`-style commit (plain push, never amend/force-push), reply on each thread with what changed, and resolve the threads via GraphQL resolveReviewThread. Decisions:

1. OTP boot check (config.py `_validate_otp_auth`): keep it. In OTP mode a non-empty env allowlist stays boot-mandatory as the bootstrap seed (the first admin must come from somewhere); the demotion means it is grant-only, and removing an env-listed address still requires the env edit — the same known cost as `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS`. Record this as an explicit amendment note to ADR 0032 decision 2 in the ADR and add a one-line "amended by 0043" pointer in 0032 (keep it minimal).
2. Auto-import: keep it (lockout is strictly worse), but make it provisional: imported rows carry `source = auto_import` (vs `admin`), the Members page shows them under a "review imported members" banner until an admin confirms or removes each, and the ADR states plainly that the import is a lockout guard, not evidence of intended membership — reconcile the alternatives-section wording so it rejects a silent migration backfill, not the flagged import.
3. 401 vs 403: state the door-specific truth — REST 403 with the membership reason; at `/mcp` FastMCP's verifier turns a resolver rejection into 401 by construction, and changing that is out of scope for this ADR (note that the audit log line is the place the reason is recorded for both doors).
4. Drop the duplicated superuser clause.

Rule 41 still applies (no `#NNNN` in docs/site). Run mkdocs --strict and pre-commit again. Report when pushed.

Branch from `origin/main` AFTER `git fetch` (PR #1890 just merged `GET /admin/health` in `backend/app/api/v1/admin.py` + `workspace_health_service.py` — read them and extend that endpoint rather than adding a parallel one).

Read before coding: `backend/app/db/models.py` (Connection — it already has `last_polled_at`/`consecutive_poll_failures`/`last_poll_error` for ORCHESTRATION connections from #839; check what exists for datasource connections), `backend/app/services/run_service.py` + `backend/app/worker/tasks.py` (where a suite run fails operationally with `error` status and how the failure reason is classified — `backend/app/services/failure_classifier.py`), `backend/app/services/connection_service.py` (test-connection path), `backend/app/api/v1/connections.py` (list response model), `frontend/src/api/connections.ts` types (you will add fields; the UI rendering is NOT in scope but keep the TS type in sync), the MCP `list_connections` tool in `backend/app/mcp/server.py` (it reports `consecutive_run_failures` — read its docstring; if your new fields make it more honest, add them there too and keep `tests/support/mcp_gates.py` untouched unless a gate changes).

Design (piggyback on run outcomes — no periodic live probe, which would spend warehouse credits and needs its own beat; record that choice in the PR body):
- Additive migration: `connections.last_auth_failure_at`, `last_auth_success_at`, `consecutive_auth_failures` (int default 0), `last_auth_error` (classified text, never raw). Backward-compatible, nullable, tested up+down on real Postgres; new revision id checked against existing ids (collisions happened twice — see `backend/alembic/versions/`).
- Write path: when a run/dry-run/test-connection/profile against a datasource connection fails with an auth-class failure (extend `failure_classifier` with an explicit `auth` class if none exists — Snowflake 250001/390100-family, Databricks 401/403 invalid token, ADLS/S3 AuthenticationFailed/InvalidAccessKeyId/SignatureDoesNotMatch/403, Iceberg REST 401), bump the counters; on a successful connection use, reset `consecutive_auth_failures=0` and stamp `last_auth_success_at`. Do this at ONE choke point (the runner dispatch / connection-open seam), not per adapter — the guard-at-one-door-not-its-sibling class is the known failure mode; enumerate in the PR body every caller that opens a datasource with a stored credential and show each goes through the seam.
- Read path: `GET /connections` list items gain `credential_health: {status: healthy|failing|unknown, consecutive_auth_failures, last_auth_failure_at, last_auth_success_at, last_error}` — `unknown` when never used since the migration (NULL both timestamps), never `healthy`. `GET /admin/health` gains `credentials: [...]` listing every datasource connection with the same shape (admin-wide). Test-connection success also stamps success (an admin re-auth should clear the signal immediately).
- Tests: classifier cases per datasource (real error strings from the drivers — look at existing fixtures/tests for authentic samples; don't invent), the seam bump/reset, `unknown` vs `healthy` derivation, list + admin endpoint fields per role, migration up/down. Mutation-check the `unknown`-not-`healthy` test and the reset-on-success test. Superuser/commit blindness (#1621): if the write happens in a worker path, prove it commits.
- Docs: `docs/site/reference/rest-api.md` rows, `openapi.json` regen via `backend/scripts/export_docs_reference.py`, changelog Unreleased entry, and a paragraph in `docs/site/guides/admin.md` (exists on main after #1891 merges — if not yet there, put it in `docs/site/guides/datasources-checks.md` connections section) explaining the three states. Rule 41: no `#NNNN` in docs/site. Do NOT edit CLAUDE.md/progress.md. Prose-to-code ≤ 0.2.
- Verify locally from `backend/`: black/ruff/mypy/bandit + full pytest (needs the compose Postgres; say so if unavailable). Conventional commits, one functionality each (migration; classifier; seam; API; docs), each ending `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Branch `feature/issue-1697-credential-health`. PR via `gh pr create` with the template, title `feat(connections): datasource credential-health signal from run outcomes (#1697)`, body `Fixes #1697`, migration checklist filled (rollback plan + tested up/down), ends `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`, milestone "v1.2 Backlog". Do not merge; do not run /code-review. Report PR URL, the caller enumeration, verification results, anything skipped.

**Option B (recommended — 3 seams, complete for stored connections):**
1. `registry.build_check_runner`
2. `profile_service._open_connection`
3. Note the sibling-door trap here: `reauth_connection:683` calls `test_connection` internally, so instrumenting `test_connection` covers reauth for free — but `test_draft_connection` has **no Connection row and no connection_id**, so your recording seam must tolerate a null subject (record it as an unattributed probe, or skip it).

- **`iceberg_credentials` is already a natural choke point** — every Iceberg credential resolution in the repo goes through `datasources/iceberg.py:457`. Free win.
- **There is no equivalent for flat-file.** ADLS/S3 secrets are resolved at 6 independent sites and passed as a bare `secret=` string into `flatfile.py` helpers.
